solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sold illicitly from sack next to stage

parts.note: to sack someone is to boot them out
a leg is a stage of a journey or race

explanation.surface: Goods sold on the quiet straight from a sack beside a theatre stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Bootleg goods are made or sold illegally, so the adjective describes anything sold illicitly.

clue.text: Check line penned by newly- wed?

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed by, so the line letter goes inside the word for the newly-wed

parts.note: a bride is a woman newly married

explanation.surface: A line written by a newly married person checking something.
explanation.definitionFit: To bridle is to restrain or keep in check, as with a horse's headgear.

clue.text: While not being filmed, Oscar, with fine female, arrived ahead of artist

indicators.note: in a down clue ahead of means placed above, so the arrival comes before the artist

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
came means arrived
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: An Oscar winner, with a fine actress, turned up before the artist, off set.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-camera describes what happens out of the camera's view, unfilmed.

clue.text: Part of particular vagrant's grub

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tramp's particular food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grub' suggests food; it is the insect sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A grub is the young wormlike stage of an insect after hatching.

clue.text: Be printed in turn on theatrical posters

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed on top of, so the turn sits above the rest

parts.note: a go is a turn in a game

indicators.note: theatrical means showy and exaggerated, so the letters of posters are put on a performance in a new order

explanation.surface: Getting your turn on the playbills of a theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'theatrical' rearranges POSTERS to TOPRESS, placed under GO.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper goes to press when it is sent to be printed.

clue.text: Brave face social worker put on

parts.note: face in the sense of cheek or nerve, which is gall
an ant is a worker in a social insect colony

explanation.surface: A courageous front that a social worker puts on for a difficult visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' reads as a job in welfare; it is the ant, a worker in an insect colony.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallant is an old-fashioned synonym for courageous or heroic.

clue.text: Enthusiasm got us in trouble

indicators.note: in trouble suggests things in disarray, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Our eagerness landed us in difficulties.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusto is hearty enjoyment or zest.

clue.text: Unconventional what injured player did?

definitions.meaning: odd or out of the ordinary, as in out of the left side
a hurt player departed from the pitch

explanation.surface: An oddball question about a player's injury.
explanation.definitionFit: Left-field means eccentric or unorthodox, and read literally it says a player went off the pitch.

clue.text: In favour of wearing article, protective garment

indicators.note: wearing means having on, so the article word goes round the word for in favour

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
pro means in favour of

explanation.surface: Supporting the wearing of a protective garment item.
explanation.definitionFit: An apron is worn over clothes to protect them while cooking or working.

clue.text: What baby's bound to do then, shortly after peg produced?

indicators.note: after puts the shortened word behind the golf peg

parts.note: a tee is a peg for a golf ball

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, so the last letter of then is dropped

explanation.surface: Asks what an infant will do once a tooth-like peg has appeared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produced' is a link; the surface reads 'peg' as a tooth, which fits the scene neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: Every infant must cut its first teeth, the process called teething.

clue.text: Gather popular judge retired

parts.note: something popular is in

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the word for the judge is read backwards

parts.note: a referee, ref for short, judges a match

explanation.surface: A well-liked judge has stepped down from the bench.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather can mean to conclude from evidence, which is to deduce.

clue.text: Working party, wanting some breakfast, ask for cereals

indicators.note: some says only part of the words that follow is taken, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A group of workers, short of breakfast, ask for cereals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' is only a link; the answer runs from the end of 'breakfast' into 'cereals'.
explanation.definitionFit: A task force is a group formed for a particular job, a working party.

clue.text: Small dog has a drink put outside, accordingly

indicators.note: the word for drinking is put outside, around the two words before it

parts.note: to lap is to drink as a dog or cat does
so means therefore, accordingly

explanation.surface: A little dog takes a drink outside, as it should.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small dog' is the definition; the Lhasa apso is a long-haired Tibetan breed, named after the city of Lhasa.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lhasa apso is a small Tibetan breed of terrier-like companion animal.

clue.text: Loud island bird

parts.note: f, forte, is the musical notation for loud
inch is a Scottish word for a small island

explanation.surface: A noisy bird living on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: An inch is a small island in Scotland, as in Inchcolm.
explanation.definitionFit: The finch is a small seed-eating songbird such as the chaffinch.

clue.text: Protagonist in love, pursuing that girl

indicators.note: pursuing means coming after, so the girl's word follows the zero

parts.note: her refers to that girl
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A lead character smitten, chasing after a particular girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pursuing' would put love after her by the surface, but the girl comes first and the love-letter O pursues her.
explanation.definitionFit: The hero is the central character of a story, its protagonist.

clue.text: In an awkward predicament immediately

definitions.meaning: put in a difficult position, under pressure

explanation.surface: Someone in a difficult position right now.
explanation.definitionFit: Being put on the spot means facing an awkward demand, and the phrase also means straight away.

clue.text: Height of distinction?

definitions.meaning: a raised piece of ground, a hill or elevation
fame or high rank, being distinguished

explanation.surface: Reads as asking for the peak of fame.
explanation.definitionFit: An eminence is both a rise in the land and a state of renown or superiority.

clue.text: Publican's secret stock inside

indicators.note: inside puts the stock word within the secret word

parts.note: inner means private or secret, as in inner thoughts
to keep is to stock goods

explanation.surface: A pub landlord's hidden supply in the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 's is a link standing for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A publican runs a pub, as an innkeeper runs an inn.

clue.text: Curry favour with eccentric queen, perhaps

parts.note: to court is to seek favour
a card is an odd or amusing person

explanation.surface: Flattering an oddball monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: A card is British slang for an eccentric, amusing person.
explanation.definitionFit: The queen is an example of a face card in a pack, along with king and jack.

clue.text: Irregular power worker

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for power in physics
an artisan is a skilled manual worker

explanation.surface: A power plant employee who works odd hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irregular' looks like an adjective, but it is a noun: an irregular soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A partisan is a guerrilla fighter, a member of an irregular armed force.

clue.text: Beginning to describe strange percussion instrument

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so the first letter of describe is taken

parts.note: rum is a British slang word for odd or strange

explanation.surface: Struggling to begin describing an odd instrument in a band.
explanation.walkthrough: RUM is old-fashioned British slang for strange.
explanation.definitionFit: A drum is the basic struck percussion instrument.

clue.text: Response from a king in receipt of bad news

indicators.note: in receipt of means taking in, so the pair receives the reshuffled letters between them

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters of news are spoilt and rearranged

explanation.surface: A monarch's reply on hearing bad news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' as the anagram signal reads in the surface as describing the news itself.
explanation.definitionFit: An answer is a reply to a question or message.

clue.text: Sophisticated city, England's capital

parts.note: urban means of the city

indicators.note: a capital letter is the first, so the initial of England is taken

explanation.surface: A refined city, England's capital, London.
explanation.definitionFit: Urbane means suave and polished, a city-bred refinement.

clue.text: Person of wealth, the French aristocrat

parts.note: a nob is British slang for a wealthy or upper-class person
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A rich French grandee described in a social column.
explanation.walkthrough: NOB is British slang for a posh or wealthy person.
explanation.definitionFit: A noble is a member of the nobility, a titled peer.

clue.text: Nerve of supporters on top of skyscraper

indicators.note: on means placed above, as in a down clue, so the undergarments come before

parts.note: bras support the bust

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

explanation.surface: Fans with the nerve to climb a skyscraper.
explanation.definitionFit: Brass is slang for cheek or effrontery, as in brass neck.

clue.text: Warplane circling about does for cargo ship

indicators.note: circling means going round, so the aircraft word goes round the short word for about

parts.note: a fighter is a combat aircraft
re is a Latin-derived word meaning about or concerning

explanation.surface: A military jet circles a merchant ship, ready to finish it off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'does for' looks like a threat in the surface (to do for is to kill) but is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A freighter is a vessel that carries goods, a cargo ship.

clue.text: Leader of gang in ridiculous feud makes unsatisfactory compromise

indicators.note: in places the gang leader within the rearranged feud
ridiculous suggests something absurdly jumbled, so the letters of feud are rearranged
the leader is the front letter, so the first of gang is taken

explanation.surface: A gang boss in a silly quarrel settles for a half-hearted deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ridiculous' rearranges FEUD to FUDE, and the G goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A fudge is a muddled compromise that avoids settling the real issue.

clue.text: Information on American group

indicators.note: on means above in a down clue, so the information word sits on top

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
US stands for American, the United States

explanation.surface: Data about a US group.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: A genus is a classification group of related species.

clue.text: Dressed warmly, wife talked volubly at college

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for wife in genealogies
to rap is to chat freely or talk at length
up means at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: A wife bundled in warm clothes chatted away at college.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'up' at Oxford or Cambridge means in residence there.
explanation.definitionFit: To be well wrapped up is to be swaddled in plenty of clothing against the cold.

clue.text: Name a song about an antelope

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so a with the word for a song is read backwards

parts.note: a lay is a song or ballad

explanation.surface: Pick a song title about an antelope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns A LAY round to YALA, after N.
explanation.definitionFit: The nyala is a spiral-horned African antelope.

clue.text: Favour method of learning involving group

indicators.note: involving means wrapping round, so the learning word encloses the group word

parts.note: rote is learning by repetition
a set is a group

explanation.surface: Preferring a way of studying that relies on group work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Favour' looks like a verb but is a noun: a badge or ribbon worn to show support.
explanation.definitionFit: A favour is a ribbon or cockade worn as a token, which is what a rosette is.

clue.text: Poor rise expected for the rest

indicators.note: poor means badly formed, so the letters of rise are rearranged

parts.note: due means expected, as a train is due

explanation.surface: A meagre pay rise is anticipated for everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' turns RISE into RESI.
explanation.definitionFit: A residue is what is left over, the remainder.
